newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia won't force foreigners to sell Gazprom.
newsitem.headline: Russia won't force foreigners to sell Gazprom.

text.p: Russia will not force current holders, including foreigners, of domestic shares in gas monopoly Gazprom to sell their stock, a spokesman for Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Wednesday.

"The rights of holders of shares in Gazprom acquired before the decree comes into force will not be cast into doubt," said Andrei Pershin, when asked to comment on market rumours that a presidential decree on Gazprom share ownership in preparation would require foreigners to sell domestic shares.

Pershin said that a requirement that foreigners sell domestic shares within three months, included in what appeared to be a draft decree sent to Reuters by banking sources, was not included in the decree under presidential review. He said the decree on Gazprom share ownership had not yet been signed.

A source close to Gazprom said the decree under consideration would allow trade of domestic shares without right of first refusal being offered to Gazprom, which is a current requirement for domestic shares, and would include a motion to be included in the agenda of the June 28 annual meeting to remove any restrictions on Gazprom shareholders rights not mandated by Russian law.

Gazprom operates a two-tier system for its shares, with foreigners required to hold Gazprom stock in the form of American Depositary Shares, share-look alikes which trade abroad but have almost a triple price premium to domestic shares.

The legal status of Russian-registered foreign-owned companies holding domestic Gazprom shares has not been specifically defined though Gazprom officials have said they are categorically against such ownership.
